steps.content: [Background - Train Corridor]
A young train attendant stands before you, with "I'm so sorry" practically written on her face. Her shoulders slump, as if this mistake rests on her alone.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: I'm truly sorry, Detective ${PlayerName}... but the last compartment was just taken by the previous passenger. There are no vacant compartments left on the train...

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: This route doesn't usually see many passengers, so we don't prepare many compartments. I never even expected we'd be fully booked today, let alone oversell tickets... Damn it, I knew that new intern couldn't be trusted...
The young attendant speaks faster and faster. Her professional smile, which was barely clinging on, finally crumbles. She grips the ledger tightly, fury blazing in her eyes.
If anger could travel through paper, that colleague who handled the registration would likely be in grave danger by now. In any case, her complaints do nothing to solve your current problem.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Pardon me, sorry to interrupt but...

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Are there any other tickets available? I'll take a hard seat if that's all you have—I can manage squeezing in for two nights. I've got urgent matters to attend to, you see, I can't afford to miss this train.
She deflates like a balloon upon hearing these words. Then comes another bow, followed by another apology.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: We have no one but ourselves to blame for this oversight, and I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience... But we simply have no room available today...

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: Let me get you registered for a ticket first. There might still be seats available in second class!
The attendant hurriedly rushes to process your ticket. The departure time is fast approaching, and the boarding bell is echoing in the far end of the corridor.
Reason tells you that reputation and dignity aren't worth missing this train over. You quickly weigh time against pride and decide the latter can be set aside for now.
Spending the night on a second-class bench won't land you in the evening papers, nor will it deal any fatal blow to your career. At worst, it'll cost you some sleep.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Sigh...
Your back certainly won't be thanking you after these two days and nights, but it seems your fate is simply sealed. You're just about to resign and accept this outcome when—
Something weighs down on your shoulder.

steps.speaker: Playful Female Voice
steps.content: There you are, darling. I was searching all over for you.

The hand rests on you very naturally, as if its owner is already used to standing by your side. You're gently guided back half a step, and before you can even turn around, a voice whispers close to your ear.

steps.speaker: Playful Female Voice
steps.content: Detective? Babe? Sweetheart? Darling? Earth to you—why are you staring at me like that?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: You're...
[Background - Clementine's Study]
You stare at the new passenger's name and furrow your brow.
Clementine.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You called?
...You wrote yourself into the story?
